fit: oral macadamia-rich formulated diet and blood lipids
assessment: The recovered original compares three oil-based diet periods using processed drinks and margarine. LDL was 0.17 mmol/L higher than the oleic period. Two participants reported transient GI discomfort. Pressing method and resting tremor were not reported.

fit: whole macadamia kernels and acute canine tremor reports
assessment: Poison-center reports include tremor and weakness after whole kernels. The same investigator observed no tremor in four experimentally exposed dogs. The overlapping series and trial are one lineage. Neither studied expressed oil, resting phenotype or Parkinson disease.

fit: independent veterinary series of whole kernels
assessment: Thirteen Australian field cases described hindlimb weakness, recumbency and pain after reported raw or roasted kernels. The case series differs from the US poison-center lineage. It supplies no separate rest-tremor outcome.

fit: topical macadamia oil and nickel dermatitis control
assessment: Pure macadamia-oil application did not significantly change skin flare or erythema in the author abstract. The comparison involved skin application and no tremor assessment.

fit: community consultation on cultural food and trade uses
assessment: The published conservation consultation records traditional uses of the kernels for food and trade. No pressed oil preparation, symptom or comparative response is described.

fit: macadamia-olive blend and gastric emptying in healthy adults
assessment: The dissertation reports the registered oil-blend comparison. Eight people entered the macadamia arm and seven contributed interpretable hydrogen transit. The groups did not differ significantly in transit response. No movement outcome or pressing grade.

fit: same oil meal in two human family-history groups
assessment: Seventeen participants per family-history group ate the same macadamia-oil meal. Postmeal metabolic responses did not significantly differ across groups. Pressing grade and tremor were unreported, and no oil-free comparator was included.

fit: macadamia oil in matched mental-health study drink
assessment: The distinct BRAVO comparison enrolled 125 and stopped early. It used macadamia-oil placebo against omega-3 and planned affect and cognitive assessments. The official registry has no posted results or Parkinson tremor outcome.

Protocol compares macadamia and coconut oils in a skin-absorption and metabolic context. Target enrollment was 16. Results and actual participant counts are absent from the official record. No food intake or tremor measure.

fit: macadamia oil as an oral krill-oil control and cognition
assessment: 555 were randomized and 245 completed. Cognition, mood and resilience did not show clear group-by-time effects. The 2019 protocol, 2021 outcomes and later trainee analysis share a cohort. No untreated arm, pressing grade or rest observation is established.

fit: unrefined oral oil and a firsthand sensory report
assessment: One person reported less numbness and tingling after unrefined oil. A copied version and serving clarification duplicate the report. The record supplies no diagnosed Parkinson disease, movement endpoint or verified cold pressing.

fit: oral oil meal and acute sleepiness and fatigue
assessment: The paper and reports describe two crossover samples of 16 and eight healthy students with separate figures. Acute alertness and fatigue contrasts do not estimate tremor. Outcome reports and the registry belong to the same family, and grade is unreported.

fit: kernel oil and tissue markers after rat chemical brain injury
assessment: The abstract reports cerebellar staining and oxidative or inflammatory biomarker changes in a potassium-dichromate rat model. Full dosing, pressing grade and denominators remain unverified. The accessible text gives no interpretable motor or tremor result.

fit: room-temperature pressed oil and alternative extraction properties
assessment: The Methods specify room-temperature hydraulic pressing. Comparative physicochemical and fatty-acid results establish process differences. The body and abstract attribute one percentage to different comparators. No participant or motor measure.
